symbols.name: encoder
symbols.summary: Ambisonic encoder. Encodes a signal in the circular harmonics domain depending on an order of decomposition and an angle.

symbols.name: rEncoder
symbols.summary: Ambisonic encoder in 2D including source rotation. A mono signal is encoded at a certain ambisonic order with two possible modes: either rotation with an angular speed, or static with a fixed angle (when speed is zero).

params.name: sp
params.description: the azimuth speed expressed as angular speed (2PI/sec), positive or negative

params.name: a
params.description: the fixed azimuth when the rotation stops (sp = 0) in radians

params.name: it
params.description: interpolation time (in milliseconds) between the rotation and the fixed modes

symbols.name: stereoEncoder
symbols.summary: Encoding of a stereo pair of channels with symetric angles (a/2, -a/2).

params.name: a
params.description: opening angle in radians, left channel at a/2 angle, right channel at -a/2 angle

symbols.name: multiEncoder
symbols.summary: Encoding of a set of P signals distributed on the unit circle according to a list of P speeds and P angles.

params.name: lspeed
params.description: a list of P speeds in turns by second (one speed per input signal, positive or negative)

params.name: langle
params.description: a list of P angles in radians on the unit circle to localize the sources (one angle per input signal)

params.name: it
params.description: interpolation time (in milliseconds) between the rotation and the fixed modes.

symbols.name: decoder
symbols.summary: Decodes an ambisonics sound field for a circular array of loudspeakers.

params.name: P
params.description: the number of speakers (constant numerical expression)

symbols.name: decoderStereo
symbols.summary: Decodes an ambisonic sound field for stereophonic configuration. An "home made" ambisonic decoder for stereophonic restitution (30° - 330°): Sound field lose energy around 180°. You should use `inPhase` optimization with ponctual sources.

symbols.name: iBasicDecoder
symbols.summary: The irregular basic decoder is a simple decoder that projects the incoming ambisonic situation to the loudspeaker situation (P loudspeakers) whatever it is, without compensation. When there is a strong irregularity, there can be some discontinuity in the sound field.

params.name: N
params.description: the ambisonic order (there are 2*N+1 inputs to this function)

params.name: la
params.description: the list of P angles in degrees, for instance (0, 85, 182, 263) for four loudspeakers

params.name: direct
params.description: 1 for direct mode, -1 for the indirect mode (changes the rotation direction)

params.name: shift
params.description: angular shift in degrees to easily adjust angles

symbols.name: circularScaledVBAP
symbols.summary: The function provides a circular scaled VBAP with all loudspeakers and the virtual source on the unit-circle.

params.name: l
params.description: the list of angles of the loudspeakers in degrees, for instance (0, 85, 182, 263) for four loudspeakers

params.name: t
params.description: the current angle of the virtual source in degrees

symbols.name: imlsDecoder
symbols.summary: Irregular decoder in 2D for an irregular configuration of P loudspeakers using 2D VBAP for compensation.

params.name: la
params.description: the list of P angles in degrees, for instance (0, 85, 182, 263) for four loudspeakers

params.name: direct
params.description: 1 for direct mode, -1 for the indirect mode (changes the rotation direction)

params.name: shift
params.description: angular shift in degrees to easily adjust angles

symbols.name: iDecoder
symbols.summary: General decoder in 2D enabling an irregular multi-loudspeaker configuration and to switch between multi-channel and stereo.

params.name: la
params.description: the list of angles in degrees

params.name: direct
params.description: 1 for direct mode, -1 for the indirect mode (changes the rotation direction)

params.name: shift
params.description: angular shift in degrees to easily adjust angles

params.name: st
params.description: 1 for stereo, 0 for multi-loudspeaker configuration. When 1, stereo sounds goes through the first two channels

symbols.name: optimBasic
symbols.summary: The basic optimization has no effect and should be used for a perfect circle of loudspeakers with one listener at the perfect center loudspeakers array.

symbols.name: optimMaxRe
symbols.summary: The maxRe optimization optimizes energy vector. It should be used for an auditory confined in the center of the loudspeakers array.

symbols.name: optimInPhase
symbols.summary: The inPhase optimization optimizes energy vector and put all loudspeakers signals in phase. It should be used for an auditory.

symbols.name: optim
symbols.summary: Ambisonic optimizer including the three elementary optimizers: `(ho).optimBasic`, `(ho).optimMaxRe` and `(ho.)optimInPhase`.

symbols.name: wider
symbols.summary: Can be used to wide the diffusion of a localized sound. The order depending signals are weighted and appear in a logarithmic way to have linear changes.

symbols.name: mirror
symbols.summary: Mirroring effect on the sound field.

params.name: fa
params.description: mirroring type (1 = original sound field, 0 = original+mirrored sound field, -1 = mirrored sound field)

symbols.name: map
symbols.summary: It simulates the distance of the source by applying a gain on the signal and a wider processing on the soundfield.

symbols.name: rotate
symbols.summary: Rotates the sound field.

symbols.name: scope
symbols.summary: Produces an XY pair of signals representing the ambisonic sound field.

symbols.name: .fxDecorrelation
symbols.summary: Spatial ambisonic decorrelation in fx mode. `fxDecorrelation` applies decorrelations to spatial components already created. The decorrelation is defined for each #i spatial component among P=2\*N+1 at the ambisonic order `N` as a delay of 0 if factor `fa` is under a certain value 1-(i+1)/P and d\*F((i+1)/p) in the contrary case, where `d` is the maximum delay applied (in samples) and F is a distribution function for durations. The user can choose this delay time distribution among 22 different ones. The delay increases according to the index of ambisonic components. But it increases at each step and it is modulated by a threshold. Therefore, delays are progressively revealed when the factor increases: * when the factor is close to 0, only upper components are delayed; * when the factor increases, more and more components are delayed. H                 THRESHOLD            DELAY 0                 1-1/P                0 OR DELAY*F(1/P) -1                1-2/P                0 OR DELAY*F(2/P) 1                 1-3/P                0 OR DELAY*F(3/P) -2                1-4/P                0 OR DELAY*F(4/P) 2                 1-5/P                0 OR DELAY*F(5/P) ... -(N-1)            1-(P-3)/P            0 OR DELAY*F((P-3)/P) (N-1)             1-(P-2)/P            0 OR DELAY*F((P-2)/P) -N                1-(P-1)/P            0 OR DELAY*F((P-1)/P) N                 1-P/P                0 OR DELAY*F(P/P)
symbols.usage: _,_, ... : fxDecorrelation(N, d, wf, fa, fd, tf) : _,_, ...

params.name: wf
params.description: window frequency (in Hz) for the overlapped delay

params.name: tf
params.description: type of function of delay distribution (integer, between 0 and 21)

io.raw: _,_, ... : fxDecorrelation(N, d, wf, fa, fd, tf) : _,_, ...

symbols.name: .synDecorrelation
symbols.summary: Spatial ambisonic decorrelation in syn mode. `synDecorrelation` generates spatial decorrelated components in ambisonics from one mono signal. The decorrelation is defined for each #i spatial component among P=2\*N+1 at the ambisonic order `N` as a delay of 0 if factor `fa` is under a certain value 1-(i+1)/P and d\*F((i+1)/p) in the contrary case, where `d` is the maximum delay applied (in samples) and F is a distribution function for durations. The user can choose this delay time distribution among 22 different ones. The delay increases according to the index of ambisonic components. But it increases at each step and it is modulated by a threshold. Therefore, delays are progressively revealed when the factor increases: * when the factor is close to 0, only upper components are delayed; * when the factor increases, more and more components are delayed. When the factor is between [0; 1/P], upper harmonics are progressively faded and the level of the H0 component is compensated to avoid source localization and to produce a large mono. H                THRESHOLD            DELAY 0                1-1/P                0 OR DELAY*F(1/P) -1               1-2/P                0 OR DELAY*F(2/P) 1                1-3/P                0 OR DELAY*F(3/P) -2               1-4/P                0 OR DELAY*F(4/P) 2                1-5/P                0 OR DELAY*F(5/P) ... -(N-1)           1-(P-3)/P            0 OR DELAY*F((P-3)/P) (N-1)            1-(P-2)/P            0 OR DELAY*F((P-2)/P) -N               1-(P-1)/P            0 OR DELAY*F((P-1)/P) N                1-P/P                0 OR DELAY*F(P/P)
symbols.usage: _,_, ... : synDecorrelation(N, d, wf, fa, fd, tf) : _,_, ...

params.name: wf
params.description: window frequency (in Hz) for the overlapped delay

params.name: tf
params.description: type of function of delay distribution (integer, between 0 and 21)

io.raw: _,_, ... : synDecorrelation(N, d, wf, fa, fd, tf) : _,_, ...

symbols.name: .fxRingMod
symbols.summary: Spatial ring modulation in syn mode. `fxRingMod` applies ring modulation to spatial components already created. The ring modulation is defined for each spatial component among P=2\*n+1 at the ambisonic order `N`. For each spatial component #i, the result is either the original signal or a ring modulated signal according to a threshold that is i/P. The general process is drive by a factor `fa` between 0 and 1 and a modulation frequency `f0`. If `fa` is greater than theshold (P-i-1)/P, the ith ring modulator is on with carrier frequency of f0\*(i+1)/P. On the contrary, it provides the original signal. Therefore ring modulators are progressively revealed when `fa` increases. H                THRESHOLD                OUTPUT 0                (P-1)/P                  ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*1/P -1               (P-2)/P                  ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*2/P 1                (P-3)/P                  ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*3/P -2               (P-4)/P                  ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*4/P 2                (P-5)/P                  ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*5/P ... -(N-1)           3/P                      ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*(P-3)/P (N-1)            2/P                      ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*(P-2)/P -N               1/P                      ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*(P-1)/P N                0                        ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*P/P=F0

params.name: tf
params.description: type of function of delay distribution (integer, between 0 and 21)

symbols.name: .synRingMod
symbols.summary: Spatial ring modulation in syn mode. `synRingMod` generates spatial components in ambisonics from one mono signal thanks to ring modulation. The ring modulation is defined for each spatial component among P=2\*n+1 at the ambisonic order `N`. For each spatial component #i, the result is either the original signal or a ring modulated signal according to a threshold that is i/P. The general process is drive by a factor `fa` between 0 and 1 and a modulation frequency `f0`. If `fa` is greater than theshold (P-i-1)/P, the ith ring modulator is on with carrier frequency of f0\*(i+1)/P. On the contrary, it provides the original signal. Therefore ring modulators are progressively revealed when `fa` increases. When the factor is between [0; 1/P], upper harmonics are progressively faded and the level of the H0 component is compensated to avoid source localization and to produce a large mono. H                 THRESHOLD                OUTPUT 0                 (P-1)/P                  ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*1/P -1                (P-2)/P                  ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*2/P 1                 (P-3)/P                  ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*3/P -2                (P-4)/P                  ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*4/P 2                 (P-5)/P                  ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*5/P ... -(N-1)            3/P                      ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*(P-3)/P (N-1)             2/P                      ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*(P-2)/P -N                1/P                      ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*(P-1)/P N                 0                        ORIGINAL OR RING MODULATION BY F0*P/P=F0

params.name: tf
params.description: type of function of delay distribution (integer, between 0 and 21)

symbols.name: encoder3D
symbols.summary: Ambisonic encoder. Encodes a signal in the circular harmonics domain depending on an order of decomposition, an angle and an elevation.

symbols.name: rEncoder3D
symbols.summary: Ambisonic encoder in 3D including source rotation. A mono signal is encoded at at certain ambisonic order with two possible modes: either rotation with 2 angular speeds (azimuth and elevation), or static with a fixed pair of angles. `rEncoder3D` is a standard Faust function.
symbols.usage: _ : rEncoder3D(N, azsp, elsp, az, el, it) : _,_, ...

params.name: azsp
params.description: the azimuth speed expressed as angular speed (2PI/sec), positive or negative

params.name: elsp
params.description: the elevation speed expressed as angular speed (2PI/sec), positive or negative

params.name: az
params.description: the fixed azimuth when the azimuth rotation stops (azsp = 0) in radians

params.name: el
params.description: the fixed elevation when the elevation rotation stops (elsp = 0) in radians

params.name: it
params.description: interpolation time (in milliseconds) between the rotation and the fixed modes

io.raw: _ : rEncoder3D(N, azsp, elsp, az, el, it) : _,_, ...

symbols.name: optimBasic3D
symbols.summary: The basic optimization has no effect and should be used for a perfect sphere of loudspeakers with one listener at the perfect center loudspeakers array.

symbols.name: optimMaxRe3D
symbols.summary: The maxRe optimization optimize energy vector. It should be used for an auditory confined in the center of the loudspeakers array.

symbols.name: optimInPhase3D
symbols.summary: The inPhase Optimization optimizes energy vector and put all loudspeakers signals in phase. It should be used for an auditory.

symbols.name: optim3D
symbols.summary: Ambisonic optimizer including the three elementary optimizers: `(ho).optimBasic3D`, `(ho).optimMaxRe3D` and `(ho.)optimInPhase3D`.

params.name: ot
params.description: optimization type (0 for optimBasic, 1 for optimMaxRe, 2 for optimInPhase)
